title: Ask, Answer, and Detect: Role-Playing LLMs for Personality Detection with Question-Conditioned Mixture-of-Experts
claim: Prior approaches map text to labels directly or with generic LLM enhancement; ours adds LLM role-play questionnaire supervision to ground predictions.
layout: 3 stacked panels (a)-(c), left-to-right flow, growing complexity toward ours
description: Three vertically stacked block diagrams compare modeling paradigms for personality detection. Each panel starts at the left with a person icon and a document icon, then flows rightward through a blue encoder box into a yellow three-circle user vector and out to a personality label (E/I, N/S, F/T, P/J). Panel (a), Traditional Deep Learning Models, is a single simple chain. Panel (b), LLM-Enhanced Text Mapping Models, adds an orange fuse box and a grey bar labeled 'LLM's generation and embedding capabilities', with upward arrows for semantic and embedding enhancement. Panel (c), the proposed model, is the most elaborate. It adds a pink stacked questionnaire card, a green Question-conditioned MoE box, a cyan answer vector, a green fuse box, and a pink Label-aware LLM Agent bar with a robot icon. Arrows are labeled Psychological Knowledge Injection and Question-level Supervision. Panel (c) holds the most colors and the most visual weight.
caption: Overview of modeling paradigms for personality detection.
abstract: Understanding human personality is important for personalized recommendation and mental health assessment. Existing personality detection methods typically encode social media posts into user representations and predict personality labels. Despite advances in large language models (LLMs), these methods face limited supervision from scarce labels and an unclear mapping between user language and psychological constructs. We propose ROME, a framework that incorporates psychological knowledge into personality detection. Inspired by standardized self-assessment tests, ROME uses LLM role-playing to simulate users' responses to validated psychometric questionnaires. These question-level answers provide interpretable, questionnaire-grounded evidence and intermediate supervision. A question-conditioned Mixture-of-Experts module jointly routes post and question representations to predict questionnaire answers under explicit supervision. The predicted answers are aggregated into an interpretable answer vector and fused with user representations for final personality prediction in a multi-task learning framework. Experiments on two real-world datasets show that ROME outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, with relative improvements of 13.60% on Kaggle and 19.72% on Pandora. Code is available at https://github.com/JasmineLyf/ROME.
